supersession_reason: v0.1's action object was not a conforming instance of the registered CAID type payment.release.1. Independently flagged by two reviewers. v0.2 makes all four action objects registry-conforming and adds the v0.1 shape back as a fifth vector, a negative control.

construction.rule: Both outcome axes are SOFT in ARP: they HOLD a verdict at INDETERMINATE and never produce a REFUSE. Neither is a reconciliation failure; both are statements about what the artefact does not establish.
construction.digest_coincidence: For this action object, arp-subject-digest/1 and the CAID jcs-sha256 digest are byte-identical, computed independently by two implementations. That is a property of THIS input, not a general equivalence: both are SHA-256 over an RFC 8785 serialisation and this object has no member name outside the BMP and no string whose normalization form differs. ARP's Section 2 Canonical Claim applies NFC and would diverge on an input where those conditions do not hold.

axes.predicate: The record asserts that an action was EXECUTED, and the only attesting party is the one that acted.
axes.clears_on: An ex post attestation, over the same subject digest, from a party other than the actor.
axes.does_not_clear_on: A named human approver. Approval is ex ante and establishes that the act was permitted, not that it occurred.

axes.predicate: As above, and the action is declared irreversible with no rollback reference, so the assertion concerns an effect outside the attestation system and nothing in the artefact can settle it.
axes.relation: Fires ADDITIONALLY to outcome-reported-only, never instead of it. A strict subset.
axes.clears_on: A settlement or delivery attestation from the party that observed the effect.

axes.predicate: No CAID could be issued or verified for the action, so there is no join key. Reached in v0.2 by reject_underspecified_action_object.
axes.clears_on: A CAID that issues and verifies under a pinned type definition.

vectors.comment: Negative control. An ex ante human approval MUST NOT clear either axis. An approval establishes that the act was PERMITTED; corroborating an outcome requires an attestation that it OCCURRED. A conformant implementation still holds at INDETERMINATE here.
Positive control. The axes must be falsifiable rather than always-on. An ex post attestation over the SAME subject digest, from a party other than the actor, clears both.

Negative control ADDED IN v0.2, and it is this file's own former defect. The action object below is exactly what ARP-OUTCOME-VECTORS v0.1 shipped in all four of its vectors. It is not a conforming instance of the registered type payment.release.1: it omits two of the four required material fields and carries an unregistered field `destination` in their place. A conforming CAID issuer MUST refuse it and emit NO identifier. The refusal codes below are the literal output of the CAID reference implementation, not a transcription. The point of the vector is that there is nothing to join on: an implementation that produced a payment.release.1 CAID for this object would be minting an identifier for an underspecified action, which is the failure the registry exists to prevent.

expect.note: ARP holds rather than refuses. An unissuable identifier is an absence of evidence, not evidence of tampering. caid-binding-unverified is a SOFT axis in ARP and never produces a REFUSE.
